Name: SupporterMod
Description: v0.15.0 - THE WARDROBE TAB, closing the everything-should-be-UI goal properly. Seventh panel tab: every wearable with a Get button - the six capes each labelled in their own colour, the three head items, the trainers - plus the slot arithmetic stated on each section header (one chest item at a time, one head item, feet use the legs slot) and the standing reminder that all of it is cosmetic, shares slots with real armour, and re-issues free forever. The chat command item maps are the single source of truth: a wearable added to a command appears in the tab with no panel change. DELIVERY RUNS ENTIRELY ON THE WORLD THREAD, because Player.giveItem reads inventory components and component access is world-thread only - the same rule updatePage taught in 0.8.2 - so the click callback hands off in one hop and does everything there. The entity Ref is resolved fresh at click time rather than captured at panel-build time, because a panel can outlive a respawn. Tab buttons narrowed 142 to 120 so seven fit the bar. Perks listings updated to name shades and trainers. 84 tests. ---  v0.14.1 - Chain and earrings removed after their live test; shades stay. The lesson, worth the changelog because it draws the boundary of what this wardrobe can sell: BODY-HUGGING ACCESSORIES ARE SKIN-DEPENDENT. The chain hung at a fixed offset from the Chest bone, but what occupies that space varies per player - cosmetic overtops are extra geometry layered over the body, and on the test player the chain sat inside their jacket with the medallion peeking out at belt height. Ear types vary the same way: fixed-offset hoops sat inside pointed ears and would float beside round ones. Push either far enough out to clear every skin and it floats beside slim ones. Things that sit ON TOP of everything - hats, capes, shoes, glasses - fit every skin; things that hug the body fit exactly one, so they are not shippable on a server where every player dresses differently. The shades landed correctly on the first attempt - the first self-authored model to do so - and stay in the headwear list: crown, cowboy, shades. Anyone holding a chain or earrings item from 0.14.0 has an item whose asset no longer exists; toss it. 84 tests. ---  v0.14.0 - THREE ACCESSORIES: shades, chain, earrings - models four, five and six, all static boxes on the proven Head and Chest bone anchors, which is why they shipped as one batch where the trainers (new animated bones) went alone. SHADES: a 32x6x2 lens bar across the eyes with amber frame and temple arms running back to the ears, black lenses with a glint. Head slot. CHAIN: gold link strands to a bar and a ruby-set medallion, hanging at the FRONT of the same Chest bone the cape hangs behind. Chest slot - and that is the honest catch stated in the delivery message: chain OR cape, one chest item at a time. EARRINGS: gold hoops at the ear positions, the smallest model yet. Head slot, hides only EarAccessory. THE SLOT ARITHMETIC, stated plainly because four accessories sound stackable and are not: every wearable occupies one of the game four armour slots, so headwear is crown OR cowboy OR shades OR earrings, chest is cape OR chain. /supporter hat now lists all four head items and says so; /supporter chain (alias necklace) delivers the chain. The jacket the same request asked for is deferred deliberately: it needs arm-bone recon - arms animate like legs did - and it competes with the capes for the chest slot, which deserves a decision rather than a default. A near-miss caught before shipping: an empty StatModifiers object crept into the new item JSONs - an unproven construct, and a rejected asset aborts the whole boot. Removed; the items match the proven cape/hat/trainer pattern exactly. Expect placement tuning on all three after the first live look, as every self-authored model so far has needed. 84 tests. ---  v0.13.1 - Trainers redesigned from one painted brick per foot to a real sneaker silhouette: a 16x3x23 chunky sole that OVERHANGS the upper by a unit all round with a cream midsole over a dark outsole, a 14x5x19 upper inset on top of it with the amber swoosh, perforated toe dots and a heel pull tab, and a 14x3x8 padded ankle collar rising at the heel with the dark ankle opening painted on top. Three boxes per foot, six in the model, all hanging off the same L-Foot and R-Foot anchors as before so the walk animation is unchanged. Same item id, same commands - capes and hats players hold keep working, and the new shape arrives with the asset pack. 84 tests. ---  v0.13.0 - SUPPORTER TRAINERS, the third self-authored model and the first ANIMATED one. Footwear lives in the LEGS slot because the game has no feet slot - ItemArmorSlot defines Head, Chest, Hands, Legs and nothing else, and vanilla boots are Legs items. That makes this the steepest cosmetic trade-off in the plugin, worth stating plainly: even the cheapest wool boots carry +13 Health and +14% resistances, so wearing cosmetic trainers costs real protection. Same rule as the cape and hats, dialled up, and the delivery message says so. The model has two root bones, L-Calf and R-Calf, each holding an L-Foot/R-Foot anchor that the walk cycle drives, with one 15x7x21 trainer box per foot - bone positions copied digit-for-digit from the vanilla Bronze legs model, because those numbers ARE the bone binding. Calves left bare and CosmeticsToHide is only [Shoes], not Pants, so trousers stay visible - vanilla leg armour hides both. Classic trainer texture: white upper, dark tread sole, laces, and the stripe in supporter amber to match the cape emblem and hat buckle. ALSO VERIFIED against a live screenshot this session: our cosmetics inherit NO stats from their wool parents - the character sheet with the cape equipped reads Health 100/100 and Defense 0%, proving a child Armor block replaces the parent wholesale rather than merging, so BaseDamageResistance 0 with no StatModifiers key really does mean zero of everything. /supporter shoes lists, /supporter shoes trainers delivers, /supporter trainers is the alias. 84 tests. ---  v0.12.2 - The perks list, /supporter info and the panel Perks tab now mention the hats - crown and cowboy, /supporter hat. Both are live-proven, which is the bar for being advertised: this plugin has held since 0.6.1 that what the perks pages claim must match what the server actually delivers, and under-advertising breaks that the same way over-advertising does. Text only, no functional change. 84 tests. ---  v0.12.1 - Cowboy hat riding higher and wider. The first live look confirmed the model renders and follows the head, and also confirmed what the hide list really does: it swaps the haircut for its FALLBACK cut - front fringe gone, exactly as vanilla helmets trigger - but this player fallback still carries its back volume, and the brim sliced straight through it. Vanilla never hits this because vanilla has no brimmed headwear; every vanilla helm is close-fitting. So the brim rises from y10 to y14 and grows 46x42 to 52x48, riding over the hair mass instead of cutting it, and the dome goes 10 to 12 tall to keep proportion. The texture sheet was re-laid-out to fit the bigger faces and the model UVs re-targeted to match. Same item id, same commands. 84 tests. ---  v0.12.0 - THE COWBOY HAT, second self-authored model and second hat design. Geometry is a 46x2x42 brim box with a 24x10x22 dome on top, hand-written against the same schema as the crown - root node Head as the bone anchor, per-face authored UVs on a 96x96 sheet, painted with a leather gradient, a rim ring so the flat brim reads as curved, a dark hatband and the buckle in supporter amber so it still reads as ours. Leather brown deliberately rather than a chat colour, because a cowboy hat in frost blue stops being a cowboy hat. THE HAT HIDES HAIR AND EARS, and that comes straight from vanilla: every vanilla helmet declares CosmeticsToHide [EarAccessory, Ear, Haircut, HeadAccessory], because a brimmed hat would otherwise have hair and pointed ears skewering straight through it. The crown keeps hair visible on purpose - it sits IN the hair and looks right there; the cowboy hat replaces it, exactly as vanilla helms do. /supporter hat now lists its designs and /supporter hat <name> delivers one - crown or cowboy - the same list-plus-variant shape as /supporter cape, with /supporter hats and /supporter crown as aliases. Same rules as everything wearable here: supporters only, zero damage resistance, re-issuable on demand, and the Head slot trade-off means no helmet while wearing it. 84 tests. ---  v0.11.0 - THE SUPPORTER CROWN, and the plugin first self-authored geometry. Hats work exactly like the cape - an armour item in the Head slot with zero damage resistance, so no combat advantage and wearing it means wearing no helmet - but unlike the cape there is no vanilla hat model under an allowed asset root (only armour helms and Halloween masks), so the crown model is hand-written: Common/Items/Armor/Supporter_Crown.blockymodel, built against the box schema read out of Violet Wardrobe beanie. The load-bearing facts of that schema, for the next model: the ROOT NODE NAME IS THE BONE - a node named Head with isPiece true anchors the model to the player head; box children hang off it; position is the box bottom-centre; each face carries its own UV offset into the texture sheet. The crown is a 34x6x33 band with four corner spikes and a front jewel in ember red, textured by tools/CrownTextureGen.java on a 64x64 sheet whose layout is ours, so no mirrored-region archaeology this time - every UV is authored. The model JSON was validated the way the manifest is - strict byte scan, not a lenient parser - before ever reaching the server, and all four AssetPackTest guards pass on it. /supporter hat (alias /supporter crown) delivers it to any active supporter, re-issuable on demand as always. ONE DESIGN DELIBERATELY: the cape went one design first too, and colour variants are trivial once the bone attachment and scale are proven in game - which is the one thing a hand-written model cannot prove from the workstation. Not yet in the perks listings or the panel; it earns that once it renders. 84 tests. ---  v0.10.2 - The whole panel scaled up, on request from a 1080p full-screen look where 720x520 filled barely a third of the screen. Window 720x520 to 960x660 and moved up (top 110 to 70), and everything inside scaled with it: body text 15 to 18, title 26 to 30, headings 20, tabs 142x42, action buttons 120x32, row pitch 38, the title field 420 wide, the trails toggle 340. The Default colour button that still clipped after the label fixes is now just Default, which also reads better next to the swatches. Also confirmed working from the 0.10.1 screenshots before this change: wearing a trail from the panel - header flips to Wearing, the row goes green with a (wearing) marker - and the hide-others toggle writing its result to the notice line. The title field and colour swatches remain the untested pieces. 84 tests. ---  v0.10.1 - Label fixes across the panel, all from the first live look at 0.10.0. CustomButtonBuilder default label style is large, bold and uppercase, so at our button widths anything past about four characters truncated with an ellipsis: STA..., TRAI..., SET..., and Wear became WE... on a 96-wide button. Every button we build now carries an explicit label style - 13px, shrink-to-fit down to 8px, no wrap - for default, hovered AND pressed states, so the whole word stays visible at every size. The colour swatches had a second bug on top: their labels reused the body text style, whose wrap=true folded #FFAA00 onto two lines and spilled the second line out the bottom of the button. Swatch labels get their own style - the swatch colour, no wrap, shrink-to-fit. The others-trails toggle also widens 230 to 280 for its longer text. Nothing functional changed; no click had even been made yet - this is what the tabs looked like on opening. 84 tests. ---  v0.10.0 - PHASE 7, step 3: Trails and Chat tabs. The panel now has six tabs - Status, Perks, Shop, Trails, Chat, About - and every player-facing feature of the plugin can be driven by clicking. TRAILS TAB: every trail listed cheapest-first with its state (free, owned, locked with its price and a pointer at the Shop tab), a Wear button on each one you can use, an Off button, and the hide-others toggle - which stays available to non-supporters, same as the chat command, because a cosmetic the people looking at it cannot switch off is a nuisance rather than a perk. Wear goes through selectTrail, the ownership-aware call the chat command uses, so the panel cannot hand out a trail the shop would have charged for. Wear buttons exist for every trail and are hidden rather than absent while locked, because editById can only edit an element that was built - and buying a trail in the Shop tab now reveals its Wear button in the Trails tab immediately, no reopen, closing the same cross-tab staleness family as 0.8.4. CHAT TAB: a text field and Set/Clear buttons for the title, colour swatches built from allowedChatColors each labelled in its own colour, and a default-colour button. All validation stays in the service - length, blocklist, allowed list - so the panel and the chat commands cannot drift. ONE FINDING WORTH THE CHANGELOG: HyUI only stores an element value into elementValues while dispatching a listener for that event type - the store happens inside the listener loop in handleElementEvents - so the title field carries a deliberate no-op ValueChanged listener. Without it the Set button would read back whatever the field was built with, forever, no matter what the player typed. Read from the HyUI source before wiring, not discovered live for once. Tab buttons narrowed 150 to 102 so six fit the bar. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.6 - Seats the crown below the shoulder mantle. The client restart confirmed 0.9.5 was right about the mapping - the crown reached the outside of the cape - but its spikes sat tucked behind a flap. That flap is real geometry: Cape1 has a child node, a 30x11 shoulder mantle that physically hangs over the top of the back panel, and a crown centred in the panel starts inside the region it covers. The crown now starts 13 rows down the panel: 11 rows of mantle plus two of clearance. No other change. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.5 - FIX: the crown was on the inside of the cape. The live test showed only three small marks near the collar, and the vanilla texture explains why: a quad DECLARES the UV region of its INNER face, and the face players actually see is mirrored to the LEFT of that offset. All of the vanilla Cape_Long art is painted in the left half of the sheet for exactly this reason. My crown, drawn at the declared offset (40,10), rendered on the cape lining facing the player back - invisible - except for its top rows, which overlapped the collar front strip (30x11 at the same offset) and leaked through as the three marks. The crown now sits in the mirrored outer region, x4..40, centred on the upper back, verified by dumping the regenerated sheet before shipping. The collar accent line was also only on the inner collar face; it now spans both. Nothing else changed - same six designs, same ids, same command. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.4 - SIX CAPE DESIGNS, each with a crown emblem. The emblem is placed from the model real UV map rather than guessed: walking Cape_Long.blockymodel quads gives exactly three visible segments - Cape1 36x35 at (40,10) is the main back panel, Cape2 and Cape3 are the sway segments below - so the crown is centred in Cape1, the upper back. Reading the UVs also explained a quiet detail: nothing samples the sheet above y=10, which is why the earlier highlight line at y=6 never rendered. Decorating outside the mapped regions decorates nothing. THE PALETTE IS THE SIX allowedChatColors, not invented: amber, frost, rose, jade, gold, ember - one cape per chat colour, so a supporter can match their cape to their chat identity and the two systems read as one family. The crown is outlined dark and filled bright so it reads on every base. Amber keeps the original Supporter_Cape item id because capes already in player inventories must keep resolving - an item id, once in the wild, is permanent; the other five are suffixed ids. /supporter capes (or bare /supporter cape) lists the designs and is deliberately visible to non-supporters, because seeing the designs is part of the pitch; /supporter cape <design> delivers one, supporters only, re-issuable in any design as often as asked - the designs ARE the perk, so there is no one-cape limit. The design argument rides a nameless usage variant dispatched on required-argument count, the standing workaround for withOptionalArg registering a named flag. All six textures and icons come from the same generator, committed alongside the output. The perks list, the info page and the panel all now mention the cape. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.3 - RESULT: there is no back slot, and the cape stays in the chest slot. The Utility item modelled on the vanilla backpack never equipped at all - what rendered was simply the HELD item slung on the player back while it was the selected hotbar slot, which is why it vanished the moment anything else was held. That is not a cape, it is a carried object, so it has been deleted. ItemArmorSlot has exactly four values and EquipItemInteraction indexes the armour container by their ordinal, so a back-worn cosmetic is not available to an item at this version. The chest cape, which works and renders properly, is now the only one. CLEANED UP: CapeSpike and /supporter capetest are gone too. That spike answered its question - model attachments DO layer - but the answer stopped mattering the moment Violet's Wardrobe showed that a cape is an item rather than a cosmetic, and an admin command that visibly strips a player clothing has no business outliving the experiment that needed it. /supporter cape now delivers one cape, re-issuable as often as asked, free to every active supporter: the entitlement is the record of truth and the item is minted on demand, so losing it in a raid costs nothing. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.2 - Testing whether the cape can avoid costing an armour slot. The chest cape works and renders, but it occupies the Chest slot, which is the one thing anybody would object to. ItemArmorSlot defines exactly four values - Head, Chest, Hands, Legs - and EquipItemInteraction indexes the armour container by their ordinal, so there is no Back armour slot to declare and no way to invent one. BUT InventoryComponent has a UTILITY section with its own capacity, separate from the ARMOR section - those are the extra slots along the bottom of the character screen - and the vanilla backpacks that render on a player back are Utility items with no Armor block at all, equipped through an EquipItem interaction. So this ships a SECOND cape modelled exactly on the vanilla backpack: same geometry, same texture, no Armor block, Tags.Type Utility, EquipItem interactions. Copying the vanilla shape rather than inventing one is deliberate - a rejected asset does not degrade, it aborts the boot, and that has already happened twice. /supporter cape now hands over BOTH capes on purpose, as a direct comparison; the loser gets deleted once we know. New guard alongside the asset-root check: every ArmorSlot in our items must be one of the four the server actually defines, because an invented slot name would fail validation and stop the server rather than just the item. 84 tests. ---  v0.9.1 - FIX: 0.9.0 would not boot the server. The cape item pointed its Model at Cosmetics/Capes/Cape_Basic.blockymodel, and the asset validator refused it - Common Asset must be within the root: [Blocks/, Items/, Resources/, NPC/, VFX/, Consumable/]. Cosmetics/ is not on that list. One rejected asset produced Asset validation FAILED with 1 reason(s) and shut the whole server down at boot, taking every other plugin with it, which is the second time a fault of mine has done that. The model now points at Items/Back/Cape_Long.blockymodel - vanilla cape geometry that lives under an ALLOWED root, so it still needs no modelling and still redistributes nobody else art. Its texture sheet is 96x96 rather than 128x96, so the generator was retargeted and the texture regenerated; the size is dictated by the geometry, not chosen. Worth recording for later: the vanilla Items/Back directory holds five cape models and no vanilla ITEM uses any of them, while backpacks in the same directory equip through an EquipItem interaction rather than an ArmorSlot. That hints at a back slot which would not cost the chest armour slot at all - a better home for this if it works, and a separate experiment. NEW GUARD, because a bad asset does not degrade, it stops the server: AssetPackTest checks that every item Model and Texture sits under an allowed root, that every texture and icon we reference is actually in the jar (a missing texture renders as nothing, silently), and that IncludesAssetPack is true whenever assets are shipped. Verified by putting the exact bad path back and watching the build fail naming it. 83 tests. ---  v0.9.0 - THE SUPPORTER CAPE. Capes turn out to be buildable after all, and my earlier verdict of not feasible was wrong because I was looking at the wrong system entirely. Violet's Wardrobe - running on this very server - ships cloaks as ARMOUR ITEMS in a plugin asset pack, which has nothing to do with the cosmetics registry, PlayerSkin or entitlements. That is why every route I investigated came up empty. The cape is therefore an item: Server/Item/Items/Armor/Cloak/Supporter_Cape.json, with our texture and icon under Common/. ZERO DAMAGE RESISTANCE, so it confers no combat advantage and stays on the right side of the line this whole plugin is built around. THE HONEST COST: the game defines exactly four armour slots - Chest, Legs, Head, Hands - and no cosmetic-only slot, so the cape occupies Chest and wearing it means wearing no chest armour. It is a cosmetic to be seen in, not an edge in a fight, and that was a deliberate decision rather than an oversight. The geometry points at the vanilla Cape_Basic blockymodel already on every client, so no modelling was needed and nobody else's art is redistributed - the same principle as the trails using stock particle effects. Texture and icon are generated by tools/CapeTextureGen.java and committed alongside it, 128x96 to match the geometry UVs, deliberately near-uniform because placing detail before knowing the UV map is how you get a crest on the inside of a hem. The item is named with a literal TranslationProperties.Name rather than a translation key, which FactionMod proves works here - Violet's had to ship a 3757-line copy of the vanilla items.lang to add 104 names, and shipping the whole vanilla language file to add one line is exactly the fragment-over-file trap that has bitten this server before. /supporter cape hands one to any active supporter, AS OFTEN AS THEY ASK. A cape is an item, so it can be dropped or lost on death, and nobody loses what they paid for - the entitlement is the record of truth and the item is minted on demand. Not yet in the token shop: the geometry reference is unverified until it renders in game, and wiring up purchases around an item that might need its model replaced would be premature. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.7 - SPIKE: two diagnostics, because appending to the live model still changed the whole character and the obvious explanation was wrong. 0.8.6 confirmed from the log that it really was appending to the live model - now 6 attachment(s) - so regenerating from the skin was NOT the cause, and guessing a third time is worse than measuring. capetest list prints the live model unchanged: asset id, model, texture, gradient set and id, scale, randomAttachmentIds, and every attachment with its model, texture, gradients and weight. That says what those five existing attachments actually ARE, which nothing so far has established. capetest noop rebuilds the live model with no change whatsoever and pushes it. That is the control: if the character still changes after a no-change rebuild, the fault is in copying and re-sending a Model - which would mean the 22-argument copy is lossy despite every field having a getter, or that replacing ModelComponent mid-session is inherently destructive - and no amount of tuning the cape attachment would ever have fixed it. If the character does NOT change, the rebuild is sound and the added attachment is disturbing the other five, which points at the weights. Nothing shipped in this version affects any player. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.6 - SPIKE RESULT: MODEL ATTACHMENTS LAYER. A cape rendered on a player who owns no cape entitlement, using the vanilla Cape_Basic geometry that already ships with every client. That was the one thing bytecode could not tell us - Model carries both a ModelAttachment array and a randomAttachmentIds map with a weight per attachment, which read like a weighted pool the engine picks one from rather than a list it renders all of. It renders all of them. Custom capes are therefore buildable: shared geometry, our texture, no cosmetics registry and no entitlements involved. FIX in the same breath: the first attempt also changed the rest of the character. It built a fresh model with createModel(skin) and appended to that, and a freshly generated model is NOT the same as the one the player is wearing - everything the live model carried beyond a plain skin build was silently discarded, which is why a cape appeared and the body underneath changed with it. It now appends to the live ModelComponent and touches nothing else. Reset still regenerates from the account skin, because that is exactly what a reset should mean. Repeated runs now swap the cape rather than stacking them: any attachment already using the cape model is dropped before the new one is added. Still a spike, still deleted before any of this ships as a feature. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.5 - SPIKE: /supporter capetest, a temporary admin command that answers one question before any cape feature gets built. Custom capes cannot go through the cosmetics system at all: CosmeticsModule reads getBaseAssetPack() rather than getAssetPacks(), so a plugin cannot register a cosmetic part, and every one of the 15 vanilla capes carries an Entitlements field naming a Hytale edition (game.founder, game.base, game.deluxe) - content people buy with the game, which a paid server has no business handing out. The server enforces none of that, by the way: validateSkin only checks the part id exists, there are zero entitlement references in CosmeticsModule and no entitlement classes in the server jar. So the route is the MODEL rather than the cosmetic registry. CosmeticsModule.createModel(PlayerSkin) builds the players Model server-side, Model carries a ModelAttachment array and is NetworkSerializable, ModelAttachment has a public constructor taking a model path and a texture path, and a replaced ModelComponent sets isNetworkOutdated to true in its own constructor so the change pushes without a setter. That means the geometry can be the vanilla cape blockymodel already on every client - the same principle as the trails using stock particle effects - while the texture is ours. WHAT COULD NOT BE SETTLED BY READING BYTECODE: Model carries both a ModelAttachment array and a randomAttachmentIds map, and every attachment has a weight, which reads like a weighted pool the engine picks ONE from for random NPC variation rather than a list it renders all of. If that is what it is, this approach dies, and it is far better to learn that from a throwaway command than from a half-built shop feature. capetest takes the texture as an argument so several can be tried without a rebuild, because the most likely failure is a texture the client cannot resolve and that looks identical to attachments not layering unless you can try more than one. Model is rebuilt rather than mutated - its fields are private and final, so the extra attachment means constructing a new Model from the old ones getters, and all 25 fields were verified to have public getters first. Delete CapeSpike and this command once the answer is known. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.4 - FIX: the Status tab kept the balance it had when the panel opened. After buying gold the Shop correctly showed 0 tokens while Status still said 200, and its list of trails owned still read heal, snow with gold missing. Neither was wrong about the database - 180 days is 6 months, 600 tokens earned, and heal 250 plus snow 150 plus gold 200 is exactly 600 spent - the Status tab was simply built when the panel opened and never told anything had changed. This is the third time the same shape of bug has been found in three builds, each one level up from the last: 0.8.2 refreshed the clicked row and left the other rows lying about their price, 0.8.3 refreshed the whole shop and left the Status tab lying about the balance. A HyUI page is a SNAPSHOT, so anything derived from state that a click changes has to be listed in the refresh explicitly or it silently keeps showing the world as it was. The refresh is now named for what it does rather than where it lives - refreshAfterPurchase, covering both tabs - and the two texts it shares with the Status tab are single methods called from both places, so a future change cannot update one and forget the other. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.3 - Shop refresh fixes, both from watching a real purchase. THE BUY BUTTON SURVIVED THE PURCHASE. 0.8.2 refreshed only the row that was clicked, so after buying snow the balance and that row updated correctly but its Buy button stayed on screen until the panel was closed and reopened - a button offering to sell something you had just bought. Every row now refreshes, not just the clicked one, because spending changes the shortfall on all the others too: buying snow at 150 took gold from need 50 more to need 200 more, and 0.8.2 left the old number on screen. Buttons are also hidden when you cannot afford the item rather than shown and refused - the row already states the shortfall, so the button was noise. The element is still built and simply hidden, because editById can only edit something that exists, so a button that might become affordable later has to be present rather than absent. ROW PITCH WAS 24 AGAINST A 26-TALL BUTTON, so Buy buttons on consecutive rows overlapped by two pixels and visibly touched. Now 30. Confirmed working in this round: the in-place balance update, the row text update, the world-thread hand-off, and the database refusing a second charge - a double-click reported already owned and the balance stayed at 0 rather than going negative. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.2 - PHASE 7, step 2: the Shop tab. Every trail with its cost, colour-coded by whether you own it, can afford it or cannot, and a Buy button that spends tokens without touching chat. Cheapest first so the free ones lead and the ladder reads as a ladder - sorted rather than map order, because the trail list is a plain JSON object whose iteration order is whatever the admins file happens to say. BUYING HAPPENS IN PLACE. A HyUI page is a snapshot, so a purchase that only wrote to the database would leave the balance and the row sitting there stale and it would look as though the click did nothing. The callback rewrites just the affected labels through UIContext.editById and calls updatePage(false). THE UPDATE IS HANDED TO THE WORLD THREAD, and that is not optional: HyUIPage.updatePage reads a Player component off the store, component reads are world-thread only, and the click callback arrives on a network thread. So the callback does the SQLite half where it stands - the service is synchronized and SQLite is safe from any thread - and hands the UI half to world.execute, the same split the trail system uses. Purchases also write a one-line result into the panel rather than into chat: a button that silently succeeds is indistinguishable from one that silently failed. Nothing about the money changed - this is the same purchaseTrail call /supporter buy has always made, with the same composite primary key on (uuid, item_id) refusing a double charge at the database rather than in a check that could race. The unlocks line on the Status tab now names what was bought instead of counting it, because 1 unlock(s) owned was the first thing anybody asked about. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.1 - Panel sizing and tab targets, straight off the first live test. The window goes from 520x380 to 720x520 with larger type throughout, because at the original size the body text sat in the top third and the rest of the panel was empty. TABS ARE NOW BUTTONS. The tab strip previously rendered as plain text, so the clickable target was the width of the word with no visible edge telling you where to aim - reported as hard to click, and correctly. Each tab now supplies its own CustomButtonBuilder at 150x36 with the vanilla hover and pressed art, so it looks clickable and behaves like every other button in the game. The header is also no longer tinted with the accent: the vanilla title texture carries enough internal detail that an amber multiply turned it into a muddy mottle. The accent stays on the title text where it reads cleanly. Note on the crash reported alongside this feedback - it was NOT the panel. The client log puts the NullReferenceException at 03:58:48 during GameLoading, immediately after ProcessJoinWorldPacket and StartJoiningWorld, while the asset pipeline was running ParticleSpawners AddOrUpdate. The client never reached InGame on that attempt, and the panel can only build in response to a command typed in game. It is a client-side asset-sync fault on first join after a server restart, and it recovered on the retry. 80 tests. ---  v0.8.0 - PHASE 7, step 1: /supporter is now a panel. One window with tabs (Status, Perks, About) instead of a wall of chat lines, opened by typing /supporter exactly as before. THE CHAT OUTPUT IS NOT REPLACED, and that is deliberate: Tebex delivers purchases from the console, which cannot open a UI at all, and HyUI is an optional dependency that may simply not be there. If the panel fails to build for any reason the command prints the same status text it has printed since Phase 1 - a player never loses the answer because a cosmetic window broke. The catch is Throwable rather than Exception on purpose, because a missing HyUI arrives as NoClassDefFoundError. NO CUSTOM ART IS BUNDLED. Every texture is one the client already ships - the same paths HyUI DefaultStyles points at - tinted with the accent colour. Shipping art would mean an asset pack in mods/, which is scanned at every boot and is exactly where the Mark.png breakage came from. The accent is not hard-coded either: it reads tagColorHex, the same value the chat tag uses, so the panel matches the tag by construction and one config key re-themes both. Compiled against the servers own HyUI 0.9.8, not the 0.9.7 bundled in another plugin here - the two turn out to be API-identical (same 219 classes, same 1428 public signatures), but that was verified rather than assumed, because compiling against the wrong HyUI is how this project earned a runtime NoSuchMethodError before. HyUI is declared in OptionalDependencies so this plugins classloader can see it at all, the same class of problem as the JDBC driver in 0.2.1 and LuckPerms in 0.6.2, and it is probed on FIRST USE rather than during setup, which is the mistake that made the LuckPerms sync do nothing for a whole session. Two constraints inherited from FactionMods UI work on this same server: addChild is immutable so every call reassigns or the child is silently dropped, and the root id is fixed rather than per-tab because a changing root id stopped HyUIs delta diff reconciling and navigation quietly died. Shop and Trails tabs are step 2 - those need buttons, and whether a button nested inside a tab reliably receives clicks is the one thing this step is meant to find out. 80 tests. ---  v0.7.4 - /supporter info now answers the question when a price is set but no store link is. That is a real state, not an edge case: the price gets decided before the storefront is built, and 0.7.3 printed the price followed by nothing at all - a player reads what it costs and has no idea what to do next. It now says to ask an admin because the store is not open yet. The fully unconfigured case is unchanged. ---  v0.7.3 - FIX: 0.7.2 would not boot the server. Not the plugin code - the manifest. Prepending a changelog entry left a literal newline inside the Description string, which is invalid JSON, and PluginManager decodes every manifest during boot: the failure throws out of HytaleServer.boot, so ONE bad plugin manifest took down the entire server and every other plugin with it. The live log shows Failed to boot HytaleServer, CodecException Failed to decode, Unexpected character. What made this ship is that the pre-flight check passed. Gson and PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json are both lenient about raw control characters inside strings, so the file parsed cleanly on the workstation and was rejected by Hytale RawJsonReader on the server. Validating with a lenient parser proved nothing. The manifest is now guarded by tests that scan the bytes rather than trusting a parser: no raw control character inside any string, no UTF-8 byte-order mark (PowerShell Set-Content and Out-File add one by default), the manifest Version matches the Gradle version, and the changelog opens with the version being built. Verified by reintroducing the exact defect and watching the build fail, naming the line. A broken manifest can no longer be packaged. No functional change from 0.7.2 - the info command and the transaction-id fix are unchanged. 80 tests. ---  v0.7.2 - Adds /supporter info: what supporter rank is, what it gives, and what it costs. Separate from /supporter perks, which lists features to somebody who already knows what this is - info is for the player who has just seen a chat tag in chat and wondered what it was. Found by watching a live session: a player typed /supporter info, got a parsing error, and there was nothing to type instead. Four different messages had been pointing players at /supporter to find out more, and /supporter shows their own STATUS - so the pointer answered a question nobody had asked. All four now point at /supporter info. The text leads with the thing that matters most on a faction PvP server: everything supporter rank gives you is cosmetic or convenience, and it does not touch combat, claims, power, outpost income, KOTJ or bucks. That is the standing rule of this whole plugin, and it is worth saying to players first rather than burying it. PRICING IS CONFIGURATION AND HAS NO DEFAULT, deliberately: two new keys, storeUrl and priceLines, both free text so any currency, any tier structure and any wording works, and a sale is one edited line. A default price would be advertised to every player the moment the plugin loaded, and a wrong price shown to a paying customer is worse than no price at all - so until they are filled in, /supporter info says pricing is not set up yet and tells the player to ask an admin, which is never untrue, and warns the admin once in the log naming the keys. Also: keys this build knows about that an existing supporter.json does not are now written into the file on load. Only ABSENT keys are added - existing values are untouched, and so are keys this build does not recognise, so hand-written notes and an admin's own edits survive a version bump. Without this a new option exists only in a changelog, and using it means telling somebody to add this key to supporter.json, which invites pasting the fragment OVER the file. That has already happened on this server once, and it failed silently: zero items loaded, no error. Best-effort by design - a config that loaded correctly must not fail startup because the disk is read-only. 76 tests. ---  v0.7.1 - FIX: the transaction id could never reach the idempotency ledger. supporter_txn has existed since v0.1.0, with tests, for one purpose - Tebex retries a delivery until the server acknowledges it, so a purchase must be applied at most once. But the ledger is keyed on a transaction id, and the only command that delivers a grant hard-coded that argument to null. Nothing could ever write a key, so nothing was ever recognised as a retry, and a retried delivery granted the days a second time. The guard was real, tested, and unreachable. Adds a three-argument form, /supporter grant <player> <days> <transaction>, dispatched on required-argument count. Configure the store to run: supporter grant {username} 30 {transaction}. A retry then reports the transaction as already applied and changes nothing, while still SUCCEEDING - a provider that sees a failure retries harder. The two-argument form deliberately keeps no transaction id, because an admin typing the same grant twice means it twice. SECOND FIX, found by testing the queued path rather than assuming it: a grant for somebody who has never logged in is queued instead of applied, and a queued grant is not written to supporter_txn. It cannot be - the ledger records a DELIVERY, and a queued grant has not been delivered and has no uuid yet; writing it early would make the claim at login look like a duplicate and silently drop the purchase. So a retry arriving before that player first logged in added a second pending row. The days were never actually at risk, because each pending row is claimed through the same duplicate check and the second one is ignored, but the retry was only recognised hours later at login, and the audit log read as two purchases. The queue is now checked directly as well, so a retry is refused at the moment it arrives. 70 tests. ---  v0.7.0 - PHASE 6: community. Adds reserved slots and the new-supporter announcement, and deliberately drops /nick. RESERVED SLOTS: when the server is within reservedSlots of its cap, non-supporters are refused at PlayerSetupConnectEvent with a readable reason while supporters still get in. This is the perk the recon marked UNPROVEN and told us not to list; Phase 0b found the event is cancellable at authentication with setReason, so it is buildable after all. Off unless reservedSlots is above 0 - a perk that turns players away must not switch itself on by accident. It reserves rather than queues: nothing holds a connection open, a refused player is asked to retry. It NEVER kicks anyone already playing, and never refuses a supporter. If the check throws, the connection is allowed - locking the server over a bug in a perk would be far worse. ANNOUNCEMENT: announceNewSupporters had been in the config since Phase 1 with nothing reading it. A first-time supporter is now announced server-wide, once - never on renewal, and never on a retried payment delivery, both covered by tests. /NICK IS NOT SHIPPED. PlayerRef has no display-name setter so the nameplate cannot change, and our chat tag WRAPS mini-chat-formatters output rather than replacing it, so a nickname would render beside the real username - two names on one line. The alternatives were showing that confusion or discarding every players rank prefix. It comes off the store page rather than shipping half-done. 68 tests. ---  v0.6.4 - FIX: player-facing commands were invisible in tab completion for every non-OP player. CommandTreeBuilder filters the clients suggestion list through AbstractCommand.hasPermission, whose first line is: if getPermission() is null return true. A command with no permission is visible to everyone - which is why EliteEssentials commands appeared for normal players and ours did not. setPermissionGroup causes a permission to be generated, so /supporter and every player subcommand were hidden from suggestions while still being perfectly runnable if typed in full. Players could use the shop and never discover it existed: nothing errored, nothing logged, the only symptom was that nobody used it. The root and all ten player-facing subcommands now override canGeneratePermission to return false - visible to all, runnable by all, which is what they already were in practice. The four admin subcommands (grant, revoke, reconcile, chargeback) keep their permissions and are still filtered individually. Verified node format for the record: thepeoplesserver.supportermod.command.supporter, with a .command. segment. ---  v0.6.3 - Adds /sup and /supporters as aliases. Found by testing as a non-OP player rather than as an admin: the first thing instinctively typed was /sup, which returned Command not found. Also documents the discoverability finding - commands RUN for every player regardless of permissions, but the command tree the client uses for tab completion is filtered by CommandTreeBuilder through hasPermission, so a command whose node has not been granted simply does not appear while typing. Players can therefore use everything and still never find it. The node follows the plugin manifest: thepeoplesserver.supportermod.supporter, with each subcommand appended. FactionMod has the same shape (thepeoplesserver.factionmod.f) and the same gap on this server. ---  v0.6.2 - FIX: the LuckPerms sync never ran. The live log shows SupporterMod reporting LuckPerms NOT found at 10:22:54 and the server enabling LuckPerms at 10:23:05 - eleven seconds later. setup() runs long before other plugins are enabled, so probing for LuckPerms there caches a wrong answer for the entire session. LuckPerms is now resolved lazily on first use (a grant or a login), by which point everything is up, and PermissionSync is always installed when nodes are configured rather than being chosen at startup. Also declares LuckPerms:LuckPerms in OptionalDependencies, which both fixes load ordering and lets this plugins classloader see LuckPerms classes at all - the same class of problem as the JDBC driver in 0.2.1. If LuckPerms really is missing, the first attempt logs a loud one-time warning naming the cause instead of silently skipping, because silently skipping means a paying customer without the perk they bought. ---  v0.6.1 - Homes are now automatic. /supporter grant only ever wrote to SupporterMods own database, so every perk gated on isSupporter switched on by itself while homes - owned by EliteEssentials and resolved through LuckPerms - did not. SupporterMod now pushes the configured nodes (luckPermsNodes, default eliteessentials.command.home.limit.10) into LuckPerms as TEMPORARY nodes expiring at the end of the grace window. Temporary is the point: a permanent node plus a removal job means two systems that must agree about when somebody stopped paying, and they eventually will not - a missed reconcile, a server down over the expiry, a crash between two writes. A node carrying its own expiry cannot drift, because LuckPerms removes it whether or not this plugin is running. Renewals use REPLACE_EXISTING_IF_DURATION_LONGER so buying more time extends the node and can never shorten it. Sync fires on grant, revoke, chargeback, the nightly reconcile, and every login - the login case both delivers gift purchases that had no UUID when bought and self-heals a node lost to a LuckPerms outage or a restore from backup. All of it is best-effort and asynchronous: a permissions write failing must never fail the purchase that triggered it, because the money has already moved, so failures are logged loudly instead. LuckPerms is an OPTIONAL dependency - absent, this degrades to a no-op and every other perk still works. 66 tests. ---  v0.6.0 - PHASE 3: homes. Delivered as configuration, not code, because EliteEssentials already owns /home, /sethome and /delhome on this server and resolves the limit through LuckPerms nodes (eliteessentials.command.home.limit.<N>, homes.limit.<N>, or unlimited). Building a second home system inside SupporterMod would mean two competing /home commands reimplementing a plugin already running. The defaultHomeSlots and supporterHomeSlots keys are therefore DESCRIPTIVE: they drive what /supporter perks tells players, and must be kept in step with the real EliteEssentials and LuckPerms values or the plugin advertises a perk that does not match reality. Verified before recommending the change: lowering the limit only makes /sethome return LIMIT_REACHED - HomeService has no bulk delete, so homes already set above the new cap are kept and stay usable, and nobody loses a home they were using. Adds /supporter perks, listing what supporters get and what the player currently has, as a single source of truth for the store page. ---  v0.5.0 - PHASE 5: tokens and the supporter shop. Supporters earn tokens for tenure and spend them on trails: /supporter tokens, /supporter shop, /supporter buy. Two free trails so every supporter has the perk immediately, four behind a token ladder. THE BALANCE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED - earned is totalMonths x tokensPerMonth, spent is the sum of recorded purchases, balance is the difference. A stored counter can be double-credited by a retried grant, drift after a crash between the write and the credit, or silently disagree with the purchase history; a derived one cannot. Same argument as total_months itself. Purchases are idempotent at the database level: supporter_unlocks has a composite primary key on (uuid, item_id) and the insert does nothing on conflict, so a double-click cannot charge twice - refused by the schema rather than by a check that could race. Closes PLAN open decision 3, chargeback vs expiry. They are different events: an expiry or revoke ends entitlement but KEEPS tenure, because the player did pay for that time and keeps the tokens it earned; a chargeback means the money came back, so /supporter chargeback removes the tenure that was never paid for and the tokens follow automatically, with no separate ledger to keep in step. Items already bought are never removed and the balance clamps at zero. Nothing here touches the bucks economy - tokens have no exchange path in either direction. Schema migration V4. 59 tests. ---  v0.4.1 - FIX: trail particles never disappeared. Of the 598 particle systems the server ships, 540 have NO LifeSpan - they are designed to be attached to something persistent such as a projectile or a torch, and spawned free-standing at a world position they simply stay there forever. The first trail list picked six of those by plausible name, and the live world ended up carpeted in glowing blobs. Defaults are now drawn only from the 49 effects with a finite LifeSpan, favouring low spawner counts because a trail emits continuously. Before adding a trail, confirm the effect expires by grepping its .particlesystem file for LifeSpan - no LifeSpan line means do not use it. tools/ScanParticles.java lists the safe set. Particles already in the world clear when the client reloads the area. ---  v0.4.0 - PHASE 4: particle trails. Supporters pick a trail with /supporter trail <name>; any player can hide everyone elses with /supporter trails off. Trails are stock Hytale particle effects chosen by config id, so no custom art is bundled and an admin can repoint or cheapen one without a rebuild. This is the most performance-sensitive thing in the plugin - it runs continuously, for every supporter at once - so four controls bound it: it emits ONLY when a player has actually moved trailMinMoveDistance since their last emit (most online players are stationary most of the time, so this is the biggest saving); the particle goes to a VIEWER LIST of players within trailViewDistance rather than being broadcast, and never to anyone who has hidden trails; maxConcurrentTrails caps the work per tick so cost does not scale with sales; and the scheduler thread only resolves the world before handing off with world.execute, so every component read and particle spawn happens on the world thread. Schema migration V3. New config keys are backfilled per key, not with a whole-map guard, so a live supporter.json that predates a trail still receives it. 47 tests. ---  v0.3.1 - FIX: the chat tag did not appear on the live server. lucko:mini-chat-formatter is also installed, also sets a PlayerChatEvent formatter, and at NORMAL priority ran after us and replaced ours. Its configured format is <meta:jobtitle> <prefix><username><suffix>: <message>, which is where the rank shown in chat comes from via LuckPerms. Winning that race by registering later would have meant discarding the rank, prefix and suffix - reimplementing another plugins job to add six characters. SupporterMod now registers at EventPriority.LAST and WRAPS whichever formatter is already in place instead of replacing it, so the line becomes the supporter tag followed by the chat plugins own output, whatever it is configured to be. If mini-chat-formatter is ever removed the delegate is simply the servers DEFAULT_FORMATTER and this still works. The chosen colour now applies to the tag rather than the username, because the username belongs to the delegate - which also means the colour shows for a supporter who has not set a title. Note mini-chat-formatter logs one cosmetic warning per boot that another plugin set the formatter; it does not re-apply, so the wrapper survives. ---  v0.3.0 - PHASE 2: chat identity. Supporters get a [Supporter] tag, an optional custom title and a chat colour, set with /supporter title and /supporter colour. The chat handler NEVER cancels PlayerChatEvent and never broadcasts anything itself - it calls setFormatter, so the server keeps ownership of delivery. That is what makes it safe alongside FactionMod: FactionMod cancels the event when a player has faction chat toggled on and re-broadcasts to their faction only, so a plugin that also cancelled and broadcast server-wide would leak private faction messages to everybody. With a formatter, if FactionMod has already cancelled then ours is simply never invoked. Titles are validated for length, control characters and a configurable blocklist - the rejection message deliberately does not name the matched word, because that would turn the blocklist into an oracle somebody can probe. Colours must be on the allowedChatColors list and are normalised to the configured spelling. Identity lives in its own table and OUTLIVES a lapse: an expired title stops rendering but is not deleted, so renewing restores exactly what the player had. Schema migration V2. 40 tests. ---  v0.2.2 - FIX: plugin data now lives in plugins/SupporterMod/ rather than the path getDataDirectory() returns, which is under mods/. The asset module scans mods/ for asset packs, so the database folder was picked up as a malformed pack and logged "Skipping pack at ThePeoplesServer_SupporterMod: missing or invalid manifest.json" on every boot. FactionMod uses plugins/<Name>/ for exactly this reason. If you are upgrading from 0.2.1, move mods/ThePeoplesServer_SupporterMod/supporter.db to plugins/SupporterMod/ to keep existing grants. --- v0.2.1 - FIX: the first live deploy failed with 'No suitable driver found for jdbc:sqlite:...' even though sqlite-jdbc was correctly shaded and META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver was present in the jar. DriverManager performs its ServiceLoader discovery once against the system classloader, and Hytale loads each plugin in its own PluginClassLoader, which the system classloader cannot see - so the driver never registers and DriverManager has nothing to return. Now connects through SQLiteDataSource, which holds the driver directly and never consults that global registry. This also keeps SupporterMod out of the way of the other plugins here that shade their own sqlite-jdbc (Windskull's Survival, Hunger and Thirst all do) rather than adding a fourth driver to a registry shared between them. Note for the record: SQLite works fine on this server - the earlier recon claim that there was no SQLite precedent was wrong. --- v0.2.0 - Phase 1 complete. The entitlement core is now wired to the server: SupporterPlugin lifecycle, the /supporter command tree, player-join claiming and the nightly reconcile job. Admin subcommands (grant, revoke, reconcile) extend CommandBase rather than AbstractPlayerCommand, because AbstractPlayerCommand requires a player and Tebex delivers purchases from the console - a player-only grant command would fail on every real purchase while working perfectly in testing. No optional positional arguments anywhere: withOptionalArg registers a named flag rendered as [--name=?], so a bare positional word is rejected as an unexpected required parameter. Startup failure is surfaced rather than swallowed - the server bundles no JDBC driver, so sqlite-jdbc unpacks a native library at first use and can fail at runtime in a way no compile check catches; if that happens every command reports the reason instead of the server booting with a silently dead supporter system that accepts grants and loses them. --- v0.1.0 - Supporter rank for The People's Server. Entitlement core only: grant, renewal, grace period and nightly expiry reconcile, backed by SQLite. Renewals extend from the existing expiry rather than from now, so buying early never costs time. Grants carrying a payment-provider transaction id are applied at most once, because Tebex retries delivery until the server acknowledges it. Nothing in this plugin touches combat, claims, power, outpost income, KOTJ scoring or the bucks economy.
